title: Composite cross-root consistency
supported_claim: On the tested same-host prototype, a platform-issued HMAC-authenticated composite checkpoint bound the exact current permit-ledger digest, reconciliation-ledger digest, permit-authority epoch, monotonic composite generation, and predecessor checkpoint such that the preregistered one-sided mutations, coordinated post-issuance mutations, stale/current mixed-era root pairs, independently valid side-root substitutions, digest/epoch field substitution, forged authentication, scope/predecessor tampering, trusted-minimum rollback, and repeated-restart mixed-state attempts all failed closed. Coordinated higher-generation current state remained live.
not_proven: Atomic commitment between SQLite state transitions and composite checkpoint issuance
Crash-safe reconciliation when ledger state changes but the corresponding higher composite checkpoint is not durably established
Atomic commitment between SQLite and a truly external checkpoint service
Protection after compromise of SQLite together with the composite key or trusted-minimum authority
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 8: composite checkpoint crash-consistency and issuance reconciliation. Test the interval between a durable ledger-state transition and durable establishment of the corresponding higher composite checkpoint, including crash/restart ambiguity, duplicate issuance, stale predecessor replay, and fail-closed recovery before currentness is re-established.
